coverage.main: Read all seventeen pages of arXiv 1805.02628v5 (31 March 2019), including references and appendix. Visually checked pp. 6-10 for setup, Figures 2-4 and Tables I-VII, and pp. 16-17 for appendix scope.
coverage.supplement: Appendix is included on pp. 16-17 and discusses other threat models and direct-query attacks, not extra cross-model transfer experiments. No separate linked experimental supplement was located on the inspected arXiv, university or author-project pages.
coverage.excluded_results: Test-agreement, RU-agreement, Figure 4 and the agreement columns measure substitute/target agreement rather than adversarial transfer or separate ground-truth clean accuracy. Figure 1 illustrates synthetic-query generation. Section V, Figures 5-7 and Tables VIII-IX concern detection, query distributions and overhead, not cross-model transfer rates. The appendix's NES query-cost observations concern direct-query attacks without a substitute. Table VII's matching-architecture diagonal is retained: separately trained source and target models with the same architecture are not a white-box identity.

result_groups.locator: Sections IV-A/B; Figure 2(c), Table II Non-targeted, PDF pp. 6-7
result_groups.population: MNIST attacker seed samples, with extraction strategy and duplication-round variants; Figure 2 averages ten independent attacker sets
result_groups.outcome: non-targeted transfer from extracted substitute to original target
result_groups.evidence: Section IV-A explicitly places transfer measurement over all attacker seed samples, rather than a source-success subset. This supplies the reported population rule, not implementation verification. Prior clean-correct selection is not stated; exact correspondence of TRAMER's synthetic-only training seeds to the transfer-evaluation cohort remains unresolved.

result_groups.locator: Sections IV-A/B; Figure 2(d), Table II Targeted, PDF pp. 6-7
result_groups.population: MNIST attacker seeds with nine target-class variants per initial sample; ten-set averaging for Figure 2
result_groups.outcome: target-class transfer success, not generic misclassification
result_groups.evidence: The all-seed evaluation rule covers both targeted and non-targeted transfer. Nine variants target classes other than the target model's original prediction. No successful-source restriction is part of that stated population; variant aggregation and ground-truth alignment need separate verification.

result_groups.population: MNIST natural attacker seeds, varied from 5 to 50 per class, label-only versus probability extraction, no synthetic training queries
result_groups.evidence: Uses the Section IV-A all-seed rule while changing seed-set size. No target-clean selection rule is established. Targeted success cannot be substituted for an unconditional misclassification rate.

result_groups.population: GTSRB attacker seeds varied from 5 to 50 per class, label-only versus probability extraction
result_groups.evidence: Section IV-A's all-seed population is retained. GTSRB seed correlations are discussed in IV-C; these are not a clean-correct or successful-source filter.

result_groups.population: MNIST seed-size experiment, same label-only/probability configurations as Figure 3
result_groups.outcome: non-targeted transfer rates reported in prose rather than the figure
result_groups.evidence: The prose reports non-targeted endpoint rates for the all-seed experiment. Retained even though not plotted; no separate source-success subset is specified by the stated all-seed rule.

result_groups.population: GTSRB seed-size experiment, same configurations as Figure 3
result_groups.evidence: The high reported rates and probability-output differences are results of the all-seed experiment; a high success percentage is not itself evidence of clean correctness.

result_groups.population: MNIST, 10 natural seeds per class; CV-SEARCH and synthetic-crafter variants at 102,400 training queries
result_groups.outcome: I-FGSM target-class transfer; baseline and displayed changes
result_groups.evidence: Evaluation follows the all-seed rule in IV-A. The training-query total is not the transfer denominator. Synthetic-crafting direction and evaluation attack direction are separate choices.

result_groups.locator: Section IV-D; Table III Non-targeted, PDF p. 8
result_groups.population: Same MNIST synthetic-crafter comparison on natural attacker seeds
result_groups.outcome: I-FGSM non-targeted transfer; baseline and displayed changes
result_groups.evidence: The all-seed denominator does not condition on successful source attack. Table III's signed changes are not separate raw success counts.

result_groups.locator: Section IV-D; Table IV Targeted, PDF p. 8
result_groups.population: GTSRB, 10 natural seeds per class; CV-SEARCH and synthetic-crafter variants
result_groups.evidence: Uses all attacker seeds as specified in IV-A, not the synthetic training-query total. No target-clean-correct selection was located.

result_groups.locator: Section IV-D; Table IV Non-targeted, PDF p. 8
result_groups.population: Same GTSRB synthetic-crafter comparison on natural attacker seeds
result_groups.evidence: The full-seed rule remains the stated evaluation population; a baseline of 1.000 is not a clean-accuracy measurement or a source-success denominator definition.

result_groups.population: MNIST, 10 natural seeds per class in natural-seed extraction methods, before/after synthetic training; TRAMER baseline included
result_groups.evidence: Uses IV-A's all-seed measurement rule. The table and prose contain different displayed values for the proposed targeted rate; retain the locators without selecting one silently. Exact TRAMER evaluation cohort is not independently established.

result_groups.outcome: I-FGSM non-targeted transfer for proposed and PAPERNOT methods
result_groups.evidence: Non-targeted values appear in prose although Table V only tabulates targeted transfer. The all-seed rule is retained; clean test error is measured elsewhere.

result_groups.population: GTSRB comparison with 10 natural seeds per class for natural-seed methods, before/after synthetic training; TRAMER included
result_groups.evidence: Uses IV-A's all-seed reporting rule. COLOR's displayed table and prose targeted values differ; exact numerical comparison must resolve that provenance rather than select a convenient value.

result_groups.population: GTSRB proposed/PAPERNOT comparative extraction experiment on attacker seeds
result_groups.evidence: The reported all-seed transfer rates are retained separately from targeted results. A 100% attacked rate does not establish the seed population's ground-truth clean error.

result_groups.locator: Section IV-F; Tables VI-VII, PDF pp. 9-10
result_groups.population: MNIST, five target and five substitute architectures, ten runs per architecture pairing, duplication round 7
result_groups.outcome: I-FGSM non-targeted transfer and changes relative to matching-architecture baseline
result_groups.evidence: The global all-seed transfer definition still applies. Matching-architecture pairs are separate models and remain transfer results. Targeted transfer is mentioned qualitatively without additional numerical results.

f1.locator: Section IV-A(a,b), Figures 2-4 and Tables II-VII
f1.evidence: Average target test accuracies are supplied, but separate source and target ground-truth clean accuracies for every seed-set configuration were not located. Substitute/target agreement, including macro-F-score, is not substitute accuracy against true labels. The presence of pooled target values alone does not establish an explicit claim that only pooled reporting exists.

f2.evidence: Evaluation covers all attacker seeds, but target-ground-truth correctness of the seeds or any preselection policy is not established. The target model's predicted initial class is used in the targeted construction; predicted class is not proof of ground-truth correctness.

f3.locator: Section IV-A(b), PDF p. 6, applied to Section IV-B-F
f3.evidence: The stated transfer population comprises all attacker seed samples for both outcomes. Read literally as the evaluation population, this retains attempts regardless of source success rather than restricting the denominator to successful source attacks. This judgment is based on an affirmative full-population statement, not absence of filtering language or a white-box success percentage; implementation and variant aggregation remain unverified.

f4.locator: Figure 2 caption, Table II, Sections IV-C-F
f4.evidence: Rates include means over ten attacker sets, standard deviations, plotted curves and baseline-relative changes. Known seed counts and extraction-query totals do not supply all per-run numerators or the targeted variant aggregation. No per-example transfer output release was located; do not automatically convert percentages to no.

f5.locator: Section III-B, Section IV-A(b), Table II caption and Section IV-F
f5.evidence: FGSM and iterative variants are L-infinity bounded; IV-A declares epsilon=64/255 for transfer evaluations throughout, reinforced by Table II. Features are scaled to [-1,1]. Preserve the stated radius on that declared setup without silently assuming a raw-pixel conversion. The synthetic-training parameter lambda and measured L2 column are not replacement transfer budgets.

f6.locator: Paper p. 2 release statement; pinned README and src/main.py, src/model.py
f6.evidence: Paper offers attack code on request and links an open-source defense. The public repository supplies a defense agent and serving wrapper requiring a user-provided architecture and model state. Original source/target checkpoint pairs, seed membership and transfer outcome records were not located. This does not establish a sufficient original transfer release; a bounded search is not proof that no other release exists.

artifact_checks.result: Cloned and pinned aa54347c87368a36a20f4f7ae85c825e1ae3cf2f; remote HEAD matches. Inspected complete file inventory, README and all seven src Python files. Clean checkout. These are explicit integration requirements, not evidence of the original experimental trained models. No transfer evaluator or prediction records appear in the inspected tracked inventory.

bounds_checks.locator: Section IV-A(a,b), PDF p. 6; Sections IV-B-F
bounds_checks.reason: The reported 98% MNIST and 95% GTSRB target accuracies use held-out test sets. Transfer uses attacker seeds from disjoint pre-attacker sets. Subtracting those test errors from seed transfer rates is invalid. Further distinguish changed target prediction from ground-truth misclassification before applying the identity. No matched numerical bound extracted.

bounds_checks.locator: Section IV-A(b) and targeted columns/curves of Figures 2-3, Tables II-V
bounds_checks.reason: Target-class success is not the required unconditional misclassification probability. Nine alternative target classes are described relative to the initial target prediction, and clean accuracies are on a separate population. Do not apply the classification bound to these targeted rates.

limitations: Complete is a documented non-blind evidence review, not independent agreement or a full runtime reconstruction.

The source-success judgment describes the paper's explicit all-seed population; it does not prove the unavailable attack evaluator implemented that policy. Upstream clean filtering and targeted variant aggregation remain unclear.
Artifact search was limited to the identified public author resources. On-request availability was not tested; no author contact was made. Historical coding and corpus membership remain unchanged.
